clue.text: Champion whiskey bar? The one in the Crown

parts.note: W is whiskey in the NATO phonetic alphabet
an inn is a pub, a place with a bar
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the monarch who wore the Crown (also the TV drama The Crown)

explanation.surface: A drinker toasts a top whiskey bar and the landlord of the Crown pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Crown' looks like a pub name beside 'bar', but it is the monarchy: ER is the late Queen's cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: A champion is the one who comes first in a contest, the victor.

clue.text: Goddess subsequently entering advanced area

indicators.note: entering says one piece goes into the space between the other letters

parts.note: then means afterwards, subsequently

explanation.surface: A goddess later steps into a more developed zone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entering' puts THEN between the two A's.
explanation.definitionFit: Athena is the Greek goddess of wisdom, an example of a goddess.

clue.text: This angry exchange standing on floor

indicators.note: in a down answer, the first piece stands on top of the second one

parts.note: a cross word is an angry word, as in 'we never had a cross word'
to floor someone is to baffle them, to puzzle them

explanation.surface: An angry exchange of words takes place while standing on the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This' refers to the very thing the solver is doing; 'floor' is a verb meaning baffle, not a surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue is self-referential: 'This' is the puzzle the solver holds.

clue.text: Case of Mauritius walnuts overturned

indicators.note: overturned says the hidden letters are read backwards
of here means drawn from within, so the letters are taken out of the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A crate of walnuts from Mauritius has been knocked over.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft gave the hidden step no signal: 'of' marks it, letters drawn out of 'Mauritius walnuts', and 'overturned' reverses them.
explanation.definitionFit: A case in law is a suit brought before a court, so a synonym for lawsuit.

clue.text: British duke pedalling furiously, gobbling wife's tart

indicators.note: gobbling says the scrambled letters swallow another piece
furiously says the letters of duke pedalling are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A British aristocrat cycles hard while wolfing down his wife's pastry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'furiously' scrambles 'duke pedalling' and 'gobbling' puts W within; the duke is just letters, not D for duke.
explanation.definitionFit: Bakewell pudding is an almond-and-jam pastry from Bakewell in Derbyshire, a kind of tart.

clue.text: Mum competed, taking on terribly hot gruelling event

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mum

indicators.note: taking on says one word takes another inside it

parts.note: ran means competed, as in a race or election

indicators.note: terribly says the letters of hot are jumbled

explanation.surface: Mum took part in a gruelling race despite the terrible heat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' scrambles 'hot', and 'taking on' places the result within the word for competed.
explanation.definitionFit: A marathon is a 26-mile running race, famously exhausting.

clue.text: Happy pedestrianised zone finally enclosed

indicators.note: enclosed says one piece sits inside another

parts.note: a pedestrianised street is car-free

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of zone

explanation.surface: A shopper is happy now the area has been closed off to traffic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' gives E, which 'enclosed' puts inside CAR-FREE.
explanation.definitionFit: Carefree means without worries, so light-hearted and happy.

clue.text: Table water in Yorkshire returned sample of bacterium

parts.note: a table of items is a list

indicators.note: returned says the river's name comes back, read backwards

parts.note: the Aire is a river in Yorkshire, England

explanation.surface: A water sample from a Yorkshire table turns out to contain bacteria.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns AIRE into ERIA; the Aire is a Yorkshire river that flows through Leeds.
explanation.definitionFit: Listeria is a genus of bacteria, so one is a specimen of a bacterium.

clue.text: American tax adviser deleting content, image online

parts.note: VAT is value added tax, the UK sales tax

indicators.note: deleting content leaves only the outside letters of adviser

explanation.surface: An American tax adviser deletes material from an image posted online.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deleting content' empties ADVISER to AR.
explanation.definitionFit: An avatar is the picture or figure representing a user on the internet.

clue.text: Fine tungsten-tipped pan

indicators.note: tipped says a piece is placed at the tip, the front, of another

parts.note: W is the chemical symbol for tungsten
OK means fine, all right

explanation.surface: A fine pan with a tungsten tip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tipped' puts W at the head of OK.
explanation.definitionFit: A wok is a round-bottomed Chinese cooking pan.

clue.text: Makes cross in church, starts off new sermon every Sunday

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: starts off takes the opening letter of each of the next four words

explanation.surface: A vicar riles the congregation in church by preaching a fresh sermon every week.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts off' gives NSES from new, sermon, every, Sunday.
explanation.definitionFit: To incense someone is to anger them, making them cross.

clue.text: Glossy appearance of fish retired chap netted

indicators.note: netted says one piece is caught inside another

parts.note: an eel is a fish

indicators.note: retired says the word for chap goes backwards

parts.note: a chap is a man

explanation.surface: A retired man shows off the glossy look of a fish he caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' looks like the chap's status, but it turns him round; 'netted' puts him in the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Enamel is a hard shiny coating, so a glossy finish or appearance.

clue.text: Craft takes high water around edge of reef, a hidden danger at sea

indicators.note: around says the reshaped letters go round another piece
craft as a verb means fashion, so these letters are worked into a new shape
edge of takes the outer, opening letter of reef

explanation.surface: A boat at high tide passes near a reef, where danger lurks beneath the waves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' looks like a boat but is the anagram signal; 'around' wraps the reshaped letters round R.
explanation.definitionFit: The great white shark is a large predatory fish lurking below the surface, a peril to swimmers.

clue.text: Sheep trapped by drain

indicators.note: trapped by says the answer is what lies caught inside the word for drain, its outer letters dropped

parts.note: a sewer is a drain

explanation.surface: A sheep has got stuck in a drain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trapped by' means the answer is held within SEWER, between its S and R.
explanation.definitionFit: Ewe is the farming term for a female sheep, so a specific example of the animal.

clue.text: Send back mushrooms starter, oddly lacking vision

indicators.note: send back says the mushrooms' name is read backwards

parts.note: ceps are a kind of edible mushroom

indicators.note: oddly lacking drops the odd-numbered letters of starter, keeping the even ones

explanation.surface: A diner sends back a mushroom starter, oddly short-sighted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Send back' turns CEPS into SPEC; 'oddly lacking' keeps TRE from starter.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectre is a ghost or apparition, a vision seen by someone.

clue.text: Yes, perhaps Genesis could be used for examples in this area

definitions.meaning: Yes is a progressive rock band, an example of the genre

definitions.text: Genesis could be used for examples in this area
definitions.meaning: Genesis is another progressive rock band, so it would be cited as an example of the genre

explanation.surface: Yes, perhaps the book of Genesis could supply examples in this field of study.
explanation.walkthrough: Yes and Genesis look like a word and a Bible book, but both are 1970s British bands.
explanation.definitionFit: Progressive rock is the genre of long, complex songs played by bands such as Yes and Genesis.

clue.text: One in desperate need of help by Friday?

definitions.text: One in desperate need of help by Friday?

parts.words: One in desperate need of help by Friday?
parts.note: Robinson Crusoe, marooned on an island, was helped by his companion Man Friday

explanation.walkthrough: 'Friday' looks like a deadline, but it is Crusoe's companion Man Friday.
explanation.definitionFit: A castaway is a person shipwrecked and stranded, like Robinson Crusoe, who needs rescuing.

clue.text: It warms bishop, gaunt, esurient, drained

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
lank means thin and lean, gaunt

indicators.note: drained empties esurient, leaving only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A thin, hungry, exhausted bishop is warmed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'esurient' means hungry; 'drained' leaves ET from it.
explanation.definitionFit: A blanket is a bed covering that keeps you warm.

clue.text: 10,000 flipping fish!

indicators.note: flipping says the characters are turned round end to end

parts.note: 10,000 is 10K, written with the digits read as the look-alike letters I and O

explanation.surface: An exclamation at 10,000 fish leaping about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' turns 10K round to K01, which looks like the answer; 'flipping' also works as a mild oath.
explanation.definitionFit: The koi is an ornamental carp kept in ponds.

clue.text: My international hotel's Greek location

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like 'my!'
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An exclamation of delight at an international hotel in a Greek city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' is an exclamation, not a possessive; cor is British slang for surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Corinth is a city in Greece, famed in ancient times.

clue.text: OMG! Sun's politics disturbed a writer on the paper

indicators.note: disturbed says the letters of OMG, Sun's and politics are mixed up

explanation.surface: A reader is shocked by the political stance of The Sun newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid; its name sets up the newspaper scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A gossip columnist writes a regular newspaper feature on celebrities' private lives.

clue.text: Bad form, pinching inventor's first idea

indicators.note: pinching says one piece grips another inside it

parts.note: 'not on' means unacceptable, bad form

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of inventor's

explanation.surface: It is bad form to steal an inventor's original idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pinching' means stealing in the surface but holding in the wordplay; 'not on' is British for unacceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: A notion is a thought or idea.

clue.text: Those missing lessons — five down — they'll go downhill rapidly

indicators.note: down means lacking, short of, so the numeral is taken away

parts.note: skivers are people who dodge school or work, a British informal word
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: Truants, five of them gone, will slide downhill fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'five down' reads like a crossword reference to 5 Down, but it means minus V.
explanation.definitionFit: Skiers race down snowy slopes at speed.

clue.text: Substitute some players at Zurich

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A team brings on a substitute for some of its players in a match at Zurich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' finds the answer across 'players at Zurich'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ersatz describes an inferior replacement, a substitute for the real thing.

clue.text: Batting knocking the stuffing out of Derbyshire lower order comprehensively

parts.note: in cricket, the side batting is said to be in

indicators.note: knocking the stuffing out of empties Derbyshire, leaving its outer letters

parts.note: the tail is cricket's lower order, the weaker batters at the end of the line-up

explanation.surface: A cricket report: the batting side thrashes Derbyshire's lower order thoroughly.
explanation.walkthrough: Derbyshire is an English county cricket team; 'knocking the stuffing out of' leaves DE.
explanation.definitionFit: To cover something in detail is to treat it thoroughly, comprehensively.

clue.text: Twelve leaving party for Japanese school

indicators.note: leaving says one piece departs from the other

parts.note: a dozen is twelve
a do is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: Twelve pupils leave a party to go to a Japanese school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school' is a school of thought, not a place of lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: Zen is a school of Buddhism that developed in Japan.

clue.text: Son caught naked left barely legible note

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
raw can mean bare, naked

explanation.surface: A son caught without clothes left a hastily written note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barely' plays on 'naked' in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrawl is untidy handwriting, a hastily scribbled message.

clue.text: Indian-style rattan door, including frames

indicators.note: frames says the outer words of the phrase surround the answer, which sits within them

explanation.surface: An Indian-style rattan door, frames and all.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'rattan door, including'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tandoori food is cooked in a tandoor, a clay oven used in Indian cookery.
